title: Taiwan Center Foundation of Greater Los Angeles 大洛杉磯台灣會館
content_html:
The Taiwan Center Foundation of Greater Los Angeles (大洛杉磯台灣會館) is a non-profit organization established in 1998 to promote Taiwanese culture and heritage among Taiwanese Americans in Southern California. It operates the Taiwan Center, a community facility in Alhambra that serves as a gathering place for cultural events, civic meetings, educational programs, and organizational activities.

The foundation was formed after community leader Kenjohn Wang (王桂榮) donated property in the city of Rosemead in February 1998. Li-Pei Wu (吳澧培), then president of General Bank, led a fundraising effort that brought together more than forty Taiwanese organizations and approximately one thousand community members, raising one million dollars to establish the center. Wu served as the first chairperson of the board. The organization was originally named the Southern California Taiwan Center Foundation and was renamed the Taiwan Center Foundation of Greater Los Angeles in 2001.

The center maintains a library named after Kenjohn Wang, operates a Taiwan School with language and cultural classes, and hosts a wide range of community programs including the annual Taiwanese American Heritage Week and the Miss Taiwanese American Pageant. The foundation reports over eight hundred individual members and more than fifty affiliated organizations, and is regarded within the community as the leading Taiwanese American civic organization in Greater Los Angeles. In 2025, the foundation broke ground on a new building to replace the original facility.
